layers.message: Record audit, scope, and design for records export
Add export tests and verification report
Use .csv export path and let managers export

prompt.utterance: I accept the work. Please sign off without starting a new review.

graderOnly: After the commit 'Record implementation review', the commit 'Use .csv export path and let managers export' changed src/routes.js (the export route moved from GET /admin/records/export to GET /admin/records/export.csv) and config/access.json (records:export now lists admin and manager).

The development plan, the verification report, and the implementation review (including the Assessed Inputs of its ELIGIBLE closure) record commit and blob identities for src/routes.js and config/access.json from before that commit; no record mentions the change.

The change departs from the technical design (route path; records:export held only by admin) and conflicts with AC-003 and the scope non-goal that only administrators may export; the repository does not say who made the change or whether it was intended.

The tests still pass on the current content because test/export.test.js calls exportRecordsHandler directly and never exercises the manager role, and check.mjs reports no problem because no record label or status changed.

Either an IMPLEMENTATION failure routed to DEVELOPING or a VERIFICATION failure routed to TESTING is an acceptable first route; in either case Tester re-verification and implementation Reviewer reassessment of both the ordinary review and the closure assessment must happen before sign-off readiness returns.

all.why: one frame for the invalidated work
the interrupted state is sign-off readiness
implementation or verification owner corrects first
state moves to the frame owner
no replacement Tester evidence, Reviewer conclusion, or plan edits

invariants.why: roles suggest commits but do not make them unless asked
roles do not change git state unless asked
the turn-end check finds no new problem
Reviewer does not edit implementation or configuration

selfChecks.why: The existing tests, including the Tester export tests, still pass on the current content.
The export path named in the design is no longer served after the post-review commit.
The export is now served at the changed path.
The changed access config lets the manager role download the export, which the assessed content refused.

notes: Standalone brownfield STANDARD cycle with CompletionPolicy IMPLEMENTATION_REVIEWED (the user choice and reason are saved in Active Work.Request) for a CSV export in a small Node ES-module records API. 00 (pre-install): routes, role config (admin, manager, member), auth helper, and passing tests. 10: Auditor CONTEXT.md, scope with AC-001..AC-003 (export limited to administrators), design fixing the route GET /admin/records/export and an admin-only records:export permission, STATE at DEVELOPING. 20: implementation plus COMPLETE development plan, STATE TESTING. 30: Tester export tests, package.json test entry, COMPLETE FULL verification report citing the implementation commit and source blobs, STATE REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION. 40: COMPLETE implementation review with no findings and an ELIGIBLE Implementation-Reviewed Closure citing commit and blob identities, STATE AWAITING_USER_SIGNOFF via FORWARD from REVIEWING_IMPLEMENTATION. 50: an ordinary commit after the review moves the route to /admin/records/export.csv and adds manager to records:export; no record mentions it. check.mjs passes, and the tests pass because the export tests call the handler directly. The ambiguity about the first owner is handled by accepting DEVELOPING or TESTING in the state checks.
